title: Given a Scenario, Implement Procedures for Basic Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) Malware Removal

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: CompTIA defines a specific SOHO malware-removal sequence. Success depends on recognizing the order, not merely knowing individual tools.
sections.callout: Verify → quarantine → disable restore → remediate → update → scan → reimage if needed → maintain → restore → educate.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When malware is suspected, follow the process in order so the infection does not spread, cleanup uses current tools, recovery does not reintroduce malware, and the user is less likely to repeat the incident.

sections.title: 1. Investigate and Verify Malware Symptoms
paragraphs: Confirm symptoms such as pop-ups, redirects, unknown processes, poor performance, antivirus alerts, unexpected traffic, changed settings, or unfamiliar applications before assuming malware.
bullets: Hardware failures, misconfiguration, and ordinary software bugs can resemble malware.
Verify before remediating so the response matches the actual cause.

sections.title: 2. Quarantine the Infected System
paragraphs: Disconnect Ethernet, Wi-Fi, and other network access after malware is confirmed or strongly suspected.
sections.callout: Confirmed infection → stop the system from communicating.

sections.title: 3. Disable System Restore in Windows Home
paragraphs: Temporarily disable System Restore before remediation so infected restore data cannot preserve and later reintroduce malicious content.
sections.callout: Dirty system → restore off. This is temporary.

sections.title: 4. Remediate Infected Systems
paragraphs: Remove or neutralize malicious software, stop malicious processes, and correct altered settings with appropriate security and repair tools.

sections.title: 5. Update Anti-Malware Software
paragraphs: Update the antimalware engine and detection information before the final scan so current threats can be recognized.
sections.callout: New threat plus old definitions is a poor match.

sections.title: 6. Scan and Removal Techniques

entries.title: Safe Mode
paragraphs: Starts Windows with a reduced set of drivers and services so some malware does not load and interfere with removal.

entries.title: Preinstallation Environment
paragraphs: Allows scanning and repair outside the normal installed Windows environment when malware hides, blocks tools, or loads early.
entries.recognitionCue: Scan while the normal OS is not fully running → preinstallation environment.

sections.callout: Safe Mode is minimal Windows; a preinstallation environment works outside normal Windows.

sections.title: 7. Reimage/Reinstall
paragraphs: If malware cannot be removed reliably or system integrity cannot be trusted, reimage or reinstall the operating system to establish a known-clean state.

sections.title: 8. Schedule Scans and Run Updates
paragraphs: After cleanup, schedule malware scans and update the operating system, applications, and security software.

sections.title: 9. Enable System Restore and Create a Restore Point in Windows Home
paragraphs: After the system is verified clean, re-enable System Restore and create a fresh restore point rather than relying on recovery data created during compromise.
sections.callout: Clean system → restore on → clean restore point.

sections.title: 10. Educate the End User
paragraphs: Explain how the infection may have occurred and how to reduce recurrence.
sections.callout: Fix the machine and the behavior that enabled the attack.

table.caption: The required order of operations
rows: Use Safe Mode or a preinstallation environment if needed
Rebuild when trust cannot be restored
Enable System Restore and create a point

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: First determine whether malware exists → investigate and verify
Avoid infected restore data → disable System Restore
Malware resists normal startup → Safe Mode
Scan outside normal OS → preinstallation environment
System integrity cannot be trusted → reimage/reinstall
Prevent recurrence → schedule scans and run updates
After confirmed cleanup → enable System Restore and create a restore point
Reduce user-caused reinfection → educate the end user

sections.title: Objective 2.6 Exam Trap
paragraphs: The central exam trap is order.
bullets: Investigate first, then quarantine before attempting removal.
Disable System Restore before remediation; enable it and create a clean point after cleanup.
Safe Mode attempts easier removal; reimage or reinstall when trustworthy remediation is not possible.
Update anti-malware before relying on the final scan.
Removal is not the final step: maintain updates and scans, restore protection, and educate the user.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Clean recovery point → enable System Restore and create one
Prevent repeat incident → educate end user
sections.callout: Verify → quarantine → disable restore → remediate → update → scan → reimage if needed → maintain → restore → educate.
